summary: @ornikar/eslint-config-typescript preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes a heavily obfuscated 727KB payload
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases (v1.3.13), unpacks it to a temporary directory, marks the binary executable, and invokes it via execFileSync against the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line, heavily obfuscated JavaScript bundle (javascript-obfuscator output: rotating string-array with a large constant table, hex-mangled identifiers, `// @bun @bun-cjs` header) whose contents are opaque and executed automatically on `npm install`. Alongside this preinstall behavior, the tarball ships legitimate ESLint config files (index.js, _shared.js, rules/) as camouflage; the declared purpose of an ESLint TypeScript config has no need for a second JavaScript runtime or an obfuscated executable bundle at install time. Fetching a non-Node runtime and using it to execute an obfuscated bundled payload at preinstall is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern used to evade Node-based inspection, and the shipped ESLint config does not justify it. This release under the @ornikar scope is consistent with a hijacked-scope or malicious publication targeting Ornikar consumers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
